name: clear-glass-lite
description: A decoupled fork of Clear Glass's provider-login shell. Real per-provider multi-account session isolation, real Greasemonkey/Tampermonkey-format userscript injection, a lightweight local capture/query API (guardian-lite, backed by the same JaaStore engine full Guardian runs on), and a genuinely extensible CLI. Zero dependency on the NEXUS system it was extracted from.
author: James Brooks (Erosmancer)
decoupling_rule: Every file in this repo imports only from within this repo, Node's stdlib, or electron. No file requires anything outside clear-glass-lite/ — this is the literal, checkable definition of 'decoupled' this fork uses, not just a description. Verify with: grep -rn "require('\.\./\.\./" . (should return nothing outside node_modules).
changelog_note: v2.1.1: real bug fix — config.js never had a side effect on load/get, so no config.json ever existed on disk until a user opened Options and clicked Save at least once. A real user reported "i dont see any configs" and was right — there genuinely wasn't one yet. Fixed with ensureConfigFile(), called at boot by both main.js and cli.js (CLI-only users get a real file too, not just GUI users), verified end to end: fresh CLI run now produces a real, complete config.json with zero prior interaction. Added interaction-contract.json, matching the project's own established convention (see guardian/interaction-contract.json) — every claim in it (19 IPC channels, 6 HTTP routes, 7 CLI commands, 5 config keys) cross-checked directly against the real code, not transcribed from memory. v2.1.0: real Guardian options and history. Added logger.js — one persistent, rotating error.log shared by main.js/guardian-lite/userscripts.js/cli.js (found a real gap while wiring it in: guardian-lite's server errors were returned to the client but never logged anywhere). Added a real, enforced retention limit for guardian-lite (0=unlimited default, oldest rows trimmed by real timestamp once a table exceeds the configured limit, verified directly). Added a Ledger panel to the hub UI — browse guardian-lite's actual captured data, per table, delete individual rows, all reading live from the store. Added `cli.js log` (view/clear the error log from the terminal) and Options-panel log view/open/clear. v2.0.1 fixed a real user-reported bug (node main.js instead of npm start) and a QA-found custom-command-shadowing-silently bug. v2.0.0 added multi-account support, real userscript injection, guardian-lite, an extensible CLI, config, and Options. v1.0.0 was login-only. All new capability across every version has been additive.

gui.note: Electron app — not visually run in the environment this manifest was written in (no display server available there); everything beneath the GUI layer has been tested directly.

cli.note: Works standalone, without the GUI running — see api_surface.cli_commands below.

files.purpose: Electron main process — window management, per-account session partitioning, guardian-lite lifecycle, all IPC handlers.
files.verified: syntax-checked; window/session/IPC code matches proven Electron patterns from the source project; GUI itself not visually run.

files.purpose: The only bridge the renderer has to Electron — contextIsolation + sandbox, no direct Node access from the page.
The provider registry — id/name/url/hosts/color per provider. Reused from Clear Glass's real registry, minus NCP-specific fields.
Account metadata (labels, connected/last-used timestamps) per provider. NOT session storage — that's Electron's native session.fromPartition.
files.verified: tested directly — add/rename/remove, cross-provider isolation, v1.0→v2.0 schema migration.

files.purpose: Loads Greasemonkey/Tampermonkey-format scripts from disk, matches by URL, injects via webContents.executeJavaScript with an idempotency guard.
files.verified: tested directly — metadata parsing, URL matching (provider-scoped script correctly excluded on other providers), injection code generation, error isolation (one broken script doesn't block others). One real bug found and fixed during testing: failed scripts were reported as succeeded.

files.purpose: GM_xmlhttpRequest / GM_getValue / GM_setValue shim for userscripts. Reused verbatim from Clear Glass — already zero-dependency.
files.verified: unchanged from source; source behavior already proven.

files.purpose: App-wide settings: load/save/get/set. Arbitrary custom keys pass through untouched, not just the documented DEFAULTS.
files.verified: tested directly — defaults, set/get, custom key persistence across reload.

files.purpose: The one place userData path resolution lives — computes the same directory whether called from Electron (main.js) or plain Node (cli.js), so both share one data store.
files.verified: tested directly — real Electron-absent fallback path confirmed correct for the host platform.

files.purpose: CLI entrypoint. Built-in commands, custom-command auto-loader, ensures a guardian-lite instance is reachable (finds a running one or boots its own) before running any command that needs one.
files.verified: tested directly — three separate real process invocations with data persisting across them, a real custom command file auto-discovered and executed against the live API, config get/set.

files.purpose: The persistent storage engine. Copied verbatim from the source project's own jaa-store.js — not a simplified reimplementation.
HTTP + SSE server wrapping store.js — /ingest, /query, /artifacts/:id (DELETE), /channel (SSE broadcast), /stats, /health. Enforces a real, optional per-table retention limit after every ingest.
files.verified: tested directly — every endpoint hit with curl, live SSE broadcast confirmed, DELETE confirmed precise, retention limit tested directly (10 rows inserted with limit 5, confirmed exactly the 5 newest survived).

files.purpose: start/stop/restart lifecycle for the server. The only guardian-lite module main.js and cli.js should import directly.
files.verified: tested directly — full start-stop-restart-on-new-port cycle, old port confirmed dead, new port confirmed serving the same data directory.

files.purpose: Hub window markup — provider list, scripts panel, Options panel.
files.verified: structure reviewed; not visually rendered (no display server).

files.purpose: Renderer logic — provider/account rendering (including the connected-account split-button UI), Options panel logic (including retention limit and log viewer), Ledger panel, scripts panel.
files.verified: syntax-checked; logic reviewed against the real preload bridge surface; not visually exercised.

files.purpose: One real, rotating (5MB) error log shared by every module with a real error path — logError/logInfo write to it, console output kept unchanged alongside.
files.verified: tested directly — write/read/clear, rotation on an oversized file, plain-string vs real Error object handling, no-recursion on a logging failure itself.

Opens the userscripts directory in the OS file manager.
Stops and restarts guardian-lite with current config — used when Options changes the port or enabled flag.
Fired after any account/provider state change so the hub UI re-renders without polling.
Real rows from a guardian-lite table, newest first — reads the live store instance directly, not a round trip through HTTP.

custom.contract: module.exports = { name, description, async run(args, api) }

extension_points.how: Add one entry ({id, name, url, hosts, color}) — the button grid, session partitioning, and status checks all read from this one list.

extension_points.where: userData/userscripts/*.js (open via the 'Open scripts folder' button)
extension_points.how: Standard // ==UserScript== / @match / ==/UserScript== format, real GM_* API available.
Export { name, description, run(args, api) } — auto-discovered on next CLI invocation.

extension_points.where: config.js's set(key, value), or guardian-lite's /ingest with a custom table name
extension_points.how: Neither is schema-locked to this app's own keys/tables — both pass arbitrary data through.

known_gaps: Electron GUI not visually run in the environment this was built in — no display server available there. Everything beneath the GUI layer is tested directly and for real.
npm link / global `cgl` install not performed — bin entry and shebang are correct by inspection.
guardian-lite has no authentication — binds to 127.0.0.1 only, which is the accepted mitigation for a localhost-only tool, not a complete answer if a project needs it exposed beyond localhost.
GM_getValue/GM_setValue are scoped per-partition (per account, per provider) — not shared globally. Matches the source shim's own documented behavior, not a regression.
